newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - British budget tax proposals.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - British budget tax proposals.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments on tax changes proposed by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown in his British budget statement on Wednesday.
ANDREW SNOWBALL, TREASURY ECONOMIST AT COOPERATIVE BANK
(after Brown announced a net fiscal tightening of 5.5 billion stg this year and 4.75 billion in 1998)--

"The net fiscal tightening is higher than the consensus...that's positive for gilts and short sterling because the market will take that view that it will take the pressure off monetary policy. Given that they've priced in a net tightening of four billion (stg), this is going to have somewhat more of an effect than expected.

"The thing people are looking at now is what the 5.5 billion will be made up of. He's said it includes the windfall tax, so if the windfall tax aims to raise more than they plan to spend, there's quite a big net tightening. So it's really crucial now to see whether this is coming from the corporate or consumer sector."
